If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-1}{x} & =\frac{\sqrt{0+1}-1}{0}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-1}{x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(\sqrt{x+1}-1)(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{(\sqrt{x+1})}^{2}-{1}^{2}}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x+1-1}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+1}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{0+1}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
